title: Observing and Quantifying Fibroblast-mediated Fibrin Gel Compaction
protocol: Prepare a stencil on Parafilm to layout the location of each explant, following the desired geometry.
Space each explant approximately 1-2 mm apart.
Attach the stencil underneath the area of the coverglass where the sample will be prepared with tape.
Thoroughly clean all components of the bioreactor using 70% ethanol.
Sterilize for 2-3 hr under UV light prior to experimentation.
Clean and sterilize alternative vessels properly if used instead of a bioreactor.
Cast a thin layer of fibrin gel on the surface of the coverglass after sterilization.
Prepare a solution of fluorescent microbeads in DMEM at a concentration of 10 million beads/ml.
Combine 0.017 ml of microbead stock solution and 0.149 ml of DMEM into a microcentrifuge tube.
Sonicate the suspension for 10 min to disperse the beads and homogenize the solution.
In a 15 ml c-tube, mix 0.22 ml of fibrinogen stock solution with 0.44 ml of 20 mM HEPES buffer.
Add 0.1667 ml of DMEM with microbeads to the mixture in step 3.1.
In a separate 15 ml c-tube, mix together 0.0328 ml of thrombin stock solution, 0.131 ml of 20 mM HEPES buffer, and 0.00246 ml of 2 M CaCl2.
Carefully mix the thrombin solution with the fibrinogen solution by pipetting up and down 5-10x until evenly distributed.
Pipette the mixed solution onto the coverglass as soon as possible to avoid gel formation delay.
Allow the gel to polymerize at room temperature.
Incubate the gel at 37 °C for 15-30 min.
Remove medium from the T-75 flask containing human dermal fibroblast cells.
Rinse the surface with approximately 5 ml of phosphate buffered saline (PBS) to remove serum proteins.
Add 1 ml of trypsin-EDTA and incubate for 3 min, or until cells have lifted.
Spin the cell suspension down in a centrifuge at 200 x g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in DMEM to achieve a final concentration of 20 million cells/ml.
Disconnect the bioreactor from heating blocks and thermocouples.
Transfer the bioreactor to a biosafety cabinet and remove the lid using aseptic techniques.
Pipette 0.3 µl of cell suspension onto the polymerized fibrin gel following the stencil pattern.
Ensure low volume micropipette tips (0.1-10 µl) are used for pipetting.
Allow cells to settle and attach to the fibrin matrix for 1 hour at 37°C.
Add approximately 5 ml of DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 0.1% amphotericin B, and 10 mg/ml aprotinin directly into the bioreactor chamber.
Condition the medium in an incubator with 5% CO2 for 2-3 hours before use.
Re-seal the bioreactor.
Use a syringe to deliver an additional 5 ml of CO2 conditioned medium via the barbed fitting on the inlet port.
Dispense the medium slowly and ensure the entire volume of the bioreactor chamber is filled.
Carefully remove bubbles that form in the bioreactor.
Supply fresh, 5% CO2 conditioned medium to the bioreactor throughout the experiment.
Set up a syringe pump with a 10 ml or 30 ml syringe filled with 5% CO2 conditioned medium.
Connect the syringe directly to the inlet port on the bioreactor lid with Luer-lock fitted sterile tubing.
Remove the male fitting and attach the tubing to the barbed fitting on the bioreactor.
Set the perfusion rate to 0.01 ml/min.
Connect modified pieces of tubing to both outlet ports and place the ends into a 100 ml beaker to collect waste.
Use a lab jack to set the heights of the inlet and outlet feeds so that a pressure differential does not develop in the bioreactor.
If a bioreactor is not available, prepare samples in 35 mm glass bottom Petri dishes with glass tops.
Maintain samples prepared in Petri dishes in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Reseal the bioreactor after sample preparation.
Reconnect heating blocks and thermocouples.
Set the bioreactor temperature to 37 °C.
Place the bioreactor on the microscope mounted motorized stage.
Position the 20X DIC objective under the view-port.
Focus the objective on the area between the three explants.
Save coordinates (x, y, and z) of this location in the imaging software.
Select the option to acquire a large image and specify the size of the area.
Set the exposure time and light intensity to the lowest values possible.
Ensure sufficient resolution to discriminate between cells, microbeads, and fibrin fibers.
Use strain tracking software for analyzing images.
Download custom MATLAB code from the specified source.
Include microbeads in the sample as a check on calculated strain fields.
Obtain images at the exact same location for accurate strain registration.
